items.description: Annual Physical Examination - complete health assessment
items.location: Halifax Medical Centre, Primary Care Clinic – Floor 1
items.notes: Doctor reviews blood work results during this visit.

MRI: Remove all metal objects (jewellery, piercings, belt buckles, hair clips).
Inform staff of any metal implants, pacemakers, or surgical clips.
Do not eat or drink for 4 hours before a contrast-enhanced MRI.
Wear comfortable, loose-fitting clothing — metal fasteners will need to be removed.
Arrive 20 minutes early to complete paperwork and change if needed.
Inform your care team of any claustrophobia; sedation options are available.
CT Scan: Do not eat solid food for 4 hours before your appointment.
You may drink clear fluids (water, black coffee) up to 2 hours before.
If contrast dye is ordered, inform staff immediately if you have an iodine or shellfish allergy.
Wear comfortable clothing with no metal fasteners.
Arrive 30 minutes early to allow time for contrast preparation if required.
Inform your care team if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.
Blood Work: Fast for 8–12 hours before your appointment (water is permitted).
Drink plenty of water — good hydration makes veins easier to access.
Bring your provincial health card and any requisition forms.
Wear a short-sleeved shirt or one with easily rolled-up sleeves.
Continue taking your regular medications unless instructed otherwise by your physician.
Avoid strenuous exercise for 24 hours before the draw if possible.
Ultrasound: For an abdominal ultrasound: drink 4–6 glasses of water 1 hour before and do NOT urinate.
Do not eat or drink for 3 hours before a general abdominal or pelvic ultrasound.
Wear comfortable, loose clothing that allows easy access to the area being imaged.
Remove jewellery or piercings in the area to be scanned.
Arrive 15 minutes early to complete registration.
X-Ray: Remove all jewellery, piercings, and metal objects from the area being imaged.
Wear comfortable clothing without metal buttons, zippers, or underwire.
Inform the technologist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.
No special fasting or dietary preparation is required.
Arrive 10 minutes early to complete registration and change if needed.
Inform staff of any prior surgeries or implants (e.g. pacemaker, joint replacement).
Echocardiogram: Avoid caffeine (coffee, tea, energy drinks) for at least 24 hours before the test.
Eat lightly — a heavy meal within 3 hours of the exam may affect image quality.
Continue all prescribed heart medications unless your doctor instructs otherwise.
Wear a comfortable two-piece outfit to allow easy access to the chest area.
Arrive 15 minutes early; the test itself takes approximately 45–60 minutes.
You may resume normal activities immediately after the test.
Mammogram: Do NOT apply deodorant, antiperspirant, powder, lotion, or perfume under your arms or on your breasts on the day of the exam.
Wear a two-piece outfit so that only the top needs to be removed.
Inform the technologist of any breast implants, prior surgeries, or breast concerns.
Bring prior mammogram images or reports if this is your first visit to this facility.
Scheduling your mammogram the week after your menstrual period may reduce tenderness.
Arrive 15 minutes early to complete paperwork.
Colonoscopy: One day before: follow a clear liquid diet only (broth, apple juice, gelatin, water — NO solid food).
Complete your full bowel preparation (prescribed laxative) starting the evening before.
Stop iron supplements 7 days before; stop blood thinners only as directed by your physician.
Do NOT eat or drink anything after midnight the night before your appointment.
Arrange for a responsible adult to drive you home — sedation is administered and you cannot drive for 24 hours.
Arrive 30 minutes early; bring your health card, medication list, and a change of clothes.
Physical Exam: Fast for 8–12 hours if blood work is included (water and essential medications are permitted).
Bring a complete list of all prescription medications, supplements, and over-the-counter drugs.
Bring any prior medical records, test results, or referral letters.
Wear comfortable, easy-to-remove clothing for the physical assessment.
Be prepared to discuss your personal and family medical history.
Write down any symptoms or health concerns you want to address during the visit.
General: Please contact our scheduling team for specific preparation instructions for your procedure.
Arrive at least 15 minutes before your scheduled appointment time.
Bring your provincial health card and a valid photo ID.
Bring a list of any current medications and known allergies.
If you need to cancel or reschedule, please call at least 24 hours in advance.
